text: Good photography starts with shutter first, which is the shutter moving to let in light. After a fast shutter speed, the camera captures a fraction of the light available, but it is enough to freeze the action. The aperture later determines how much light enters the camera. The aperture is larger when you are using a darker setting and smaller when you are using a lighter setting. If you set a small aperture, the camera can capture more light but will use slower shutter speeds, while a larger aperture will allow more light to enter and will use faster shutter speeds.
